'''Joan Beringer''' ({{IPAc-en|j|oʊ|ˈ|a:|n|_|ˌ|b|ɛər|ɪ|n|ˈ|ʒ|eɪ}} {{Respell|yoh|AHN|_|BAIR|in|ZHAY}}, {{IPA|fr|jɔan beʁɛ̃ʒe|lang}}; born 11 November 2006) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

==Early life==
Beringer was born on 11 November 2006,<ref name="FIBA Basketball">{{cite web |title=Joan Beringer (France) - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/367077-joan-beringer |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=7 March 2025}}</ref> in [[Sélestat]], France.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite web |title=How to go first time playing to projected first round draft pick in 3 years? Ask Joan Beringer - FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2025 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-u19-basketball-world-cup-2025/news/how-to-go-first-time-playing-to-projected-first-round-draft-pick-in-3-years |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=7 March 2025 |date=7 February 2025 |quote=Beringer was born in Sélestat, where he lived until he was 10 and moved to Strasbourg.}}</ref> His father is [[Alsace|Alsatian]] and his mother is from Benin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dna.fr/sport/2025/06/15/la-meteorite-joan-beringer-prete-a-eblouir-le-ciel-de-la-nba|title=Basket-ball. La météorite alsacienne Joan Beringer, prête à éblouir le ciel de la NBA|date=June 15, 2025|website=www.dna.fr}}</ref> He spent the first 10 years of his life in Sélestat before moving to [[Strasbourg]]. He played [[Association football|football]] growing up, and by the summer of 2021 had "never even touched a [[basketball]]."<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bebasket.fr/joan-beringer-le-nouvel-ovni-francais-un-premier-tour-de-draft-nba-faconne-en-moins-de-quatre-ans|website=BeBasket.fr|language=French|title=Joan Beringer, le nouvel OVNI français : un premier tour de Draft NBA façonné en moins de quatre ans ?!|trans-title=Joan Beringer, the new French UFO: a first round of NBA Draft shaped in less than four years?!|author=Lacoste, Alexandre|date=23 January 2025}}</ref> However, he said that "At around 14–15 years old, I couldn't find [[Football boot|cleats]] in my size, my feet were too big."<ref name="auto"/> After being pressured by friends, he tried out basketball for the first time and enjoyed the sport. He later joined the club Strasbourg Saint-Joseph Basket and played for the U17 team.<ref name="auto"/>

Beringer joined [[SIG Strasbourg]] in 2022 and played for their U18 squad in the {{ill|LNB Espoirs|fr|Championnat de France de basket-ball Espoirs}} league, averaging 4.1 points in the 2022–23 season, then 17.4 points in 2023–24. He also played for the U21 prospects team and averaged 9.4 points, eight rebounds, and 1.5 assists per game.<ref name="auto"/>

==Professional career==
Beringer moved to [[Ljubljana]] in the summer of 2024 to join the club [[KK Cedevita Olimpija|Cedevita Olimpija]]. He was initially set to play for the club's reserve squad, but impressed and was promoted to the senior team before having appeared in a game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cedevita.olimpija.com/en/joan-beringer-signs-first-professional-contract/|publisher=[[KK Cedevita Olimpija|Cedevita Olimpija]]|title=Joan Beringer Signs First Professional Contract|date=19 November 2024}}</ref> In November 2024, he signed a four-year contract with Cedevita.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dna.fr/sport/2024/11/19/le-selestadien-joan-beringer-signe-son-premier-contrat-pro-avec-ljubljana|newspaper=[[Les Dernières Nouvelles d'Alsace]]|language=French|trans-title=Alsatian Joan Beringer signs his first professional contract with Ljubljana|title=L'Alsacien Joan Beringer signe son premier contrat pro avec Ljubljana|date=19 November 2024}}</ref> He saw significant playing time and helped them win the [[Slovenian Basketball Cup]] for the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bebasket.fr/une-emotion-enorme-joan-beringer-soffre-son-premier-trophee-professionnel|website=BeBasket.fr|language=French|title="Une émotion énorme" : Joan Beringer s'offre son premier trophée professionel!|trans-title=“A huge emotion”: Joan Beringer wins his first professional trophy!|date=20 February 2025|author=Lacoste, Alexandre}}</ref>

Beringer was selected 17th in the [[2025 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/prospect-profiles/nba-draft-scouting-report-france-joan-beringer|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=NBA Draft Scouting Report: France's Joan Beringer|date=29 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |author=Bernucca |first=Andrew |date=29 January 2025 |title=Joan Beringer Has the Skillset To Become the Defensive Anchor NBA Teams Desire |url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/joan-beringer-skillset-nba-defensive-anchor-draft |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> He debuted for the Timberwolves in the [[2025 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Ragatz |first=Will |date=11 July 2025 |title=Timberwolves react to Joan Beringer's 'incredible' Summer League debut |url=https://www.si.com/nba/timberwolves/minnesota-timberwolves-news/timberwolves-react-to-joan-beringer-incredible-summer-league-debut |access-date=17 July 2025 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> On 12 April 2026, Beringer put up a double-double with a career-high 24 points and a career-high 12 rebounds, along with a career-high seven blocks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/minnesota-timberwolves/timberwolves-news-rookie-joan-beringer-team-history-season-finale|title=Timberwolves rookie makes franchise history with big stat line in season finale|website=ClutchPoints|last=Mariano|first=Paolo|date=April 12, 2026|access-date=April 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/timberwolves-joan-beringer-double-double-with-seven-blocks/|website=CBS Sports|title=Timberwolves' Joan Beringer: Double-double with seven blocks|date=April 12, 2026|access-date=April 12, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
Beringer competed for France at the [[2023 FIBA U18 European Championship]].<ref name="auto"/>
